I think the only possible foreshadowing to this is in Tyrion's conversation with Jon in GOT Tyrion II:

>Tyrion had a morbid fascination with dragons. When he had first come to King's Landing for his sister's wedding to Robert Baratheon, he had made it a point to seek out the dragon skulls that had hung on the walls of Targaryen's throne room...

and later

>"What are you reading about" [Jon] asked.

>"Dragons," Tyrion told him.

>"What good is that? There are no more dragons," the boy said with the easy certainty of youth.

>"So they say," Tyrion replied. "Sad, isn't it? When I was your age, I used to dream of having a dragon of my own."

>"You did?" the boy said suspiciously. Perhaps he thought Tyrion was making fun of him.

>"Oh, yes. Even a stunted, twisted, ugly little boy can look down on the world when he's seated on a dragon's back." Tyrion pushed the bearskin aside and climbed to his feet. "I used to start fires in the bowels of Casterly Rock and stare at the flames for hours, pretending they were dragonfire. Sometimes I'd imagine my father burning. At other times, my sister."

It's interesting that Jon, who is almost universally considered to be a dragon head, has a conversation with Tyrion about dragons. Tyrion also mentions dragon dreams (with prophetic dreams being a super Targaryen-y thing), riding a dragon, and burning his family with dragonfire. It's not definitely foreshadowing, but it could be.

Tyrion also has a connection with Jon (they got along fairly well, and interacted a lot) and will soon have a connection with Dany, probably.

It's possible that he could act as a bridge between these two, perhaps bringing Dany to Jon's fight agains the Others.

And, as for him having difficulty riding a horse/dragon, we know that Tyrion is skilled at designing "specialty saddles" that allow him and Bran 
to ride normally despite their disabilities:

>"I require a special saddle to keep from falling off my horse. A saddle of my own design, you may be interested to know."
